nodes.summary: If $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and the interval $[a, b]$ has a partition, then $a \le b$.
nodes.title: Endpoints of a partition are ordered

nodes.summary: Let $a, b$ be real numbers. For any two tagged partitions $T_1$ and $T_2$ of $[a, b]$, there is a tagged partition $T''$ of $[a, b]$ that is a tagged refinement of both $T_1$ and $T_2$.
nodes.title: Common refinement of two tagged partitions

nodes.summary: For partitions $P$ and $Q$ of $[a, b]$, $Q$ is a refinement of $P$ when every point of $P$ is a point of $Q$, that is, when the point set of $P$ is contained in the point set of $Q$.
nodes.title: Refinement of a partition

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ with points $a = x_0 < \dots < x_n = b$ and $a = x'_0 < \dots < x'_{n'} = b$ respectively. Tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$ consist of a map $\sigma$ assigning to each index $j < n'$ an index $\sigma(j) < n$ such that $x_{\sigma(j)} \le x'_j$ and $x'_{j+1} \le x_{\sigma(j)+1}$ for every $j < n'$ (so the $j$-th subinterval of $T'$ lies in the $\sigma(j)$-th…
nodes.title: Tagged-refinement data

nodes.summary: Let $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ be a partition of $[a, b]$. Then for every $i$ with $0 \le i < n$, the subinterval length $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is at most the mesh of the partition.
nodes.title: Subinterval lengths are at most the mesh

nodes.summary: If $a < b$, then every partition of $[a, b]$ has strictly positive mesh.
nodes.title: The mesh is positive on a nondegenerate interval

nodes.summary: The mesh (also called the norm) of a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ is the maximum subinterval length $\max_{1 \le k \le n} (x_k - x_{k-1})$ when $n \ge 1$, and $0$ when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Mesh of a partition

nodes.summary: If $a < b$, then every partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ has at least one subinterval, that is, $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: A partition of a nondegenerate interval has a subinterval

nodes.summary: Let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ such that every point of $T$ is a point of $T'$. Then tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$ exist: an assignment of each subinterval of $T'$ to a subinterval of $T$ that contains it, such that for each subinterval of $T$ the lengths of the subintervals of $T'$ assigned to it add up to its length.
nodes.title: Refinements carry tagged-refinement data

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, a partition of the closed interval $[a, b]$ consists of a natural number $n$, the number of subintervals, together with $n + 1$ points forming a strictly increasing sequence $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$.
nodes.title: Partition of an interval

nodes.summary: The point set of a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ is the set of its points $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$.
nodes.title: Points of a partition

nodes.summary: For every real constant $c$ and every tagged partition of $[a, b]$, the Riemann sum of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ equals $c(b - a)$.
nodes.title: Riemann sum of a constant function

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $T$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with points $x_0 < \dots < x_n$ and tags $\xi_0, \dots, \xi_{n-1}$, and let $T'$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with points $x'_0 < \dots < x'_{n'}$, together with tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$ assigning to each $j < n'$ an index $\sigma(j) < n$. Then the Riemann sum $S_f(T)$ of $f$ over $T$ satisfies
nodes.title: Riemann sum regrouped over a refinement

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with no subintervals, the Riemann sum of $f$ is $0$, since it is an empty sum.
nodes.title: Riemann sum over a trivial partition

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $T_1$, $T_2$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ with meshes $\|T_1\|$ and $\|T_2\|$. Suppose $\omega_1, \omega_2 \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy, for $i = 1, 2$, $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega_i$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \|T_i\|$. Let $T''$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ together with tagged-refinement data from $T_1$ to $T''$ and from $T_2$ to $T''$. Writing…
nodes.title: Riemann sums of two partitions with a common refinement

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ such that every point of $T$ is a point of $T'$, and let $\omega \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \|T\|$, where $\|T\|$ is the mesh of $T$. Writing $S_f(T)$ for the Riemann sum of $f$ over $T$, we have $|S_f(T) - S_f(T')| \le \omega (b - a)$.
nodes.title: Riemann sums under refinement

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, let $T$ and $T'$ be tagged partitions of $[a, b]$ together with tagged-refinement data from $T$ to $T'$, and let $\omega \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $|f(x) - f(y)| \le \omega$ for all $x, y \in [a, b]$ with $|x - y| \le \|T\|$, where $\|T\|$ is the mesh of $T$. Writing $S_f(T)$ for the Riemann sum of $f$ over $T$, we have $|S_f(T) - S_f(T')| \le \omega (b - a)$.
nodes.title: Riemann sums under refinement, given refinement data

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $T$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$, with points $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ and tags $\xi_k \in [x_{k-1}, x_k]$ for $k = 1, \dots, n$. The Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $T$ is $S_f(x, \xi) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} f(\xi_k)\,(x_k - x_{k-1})$ (an empty sum, equal to $0$, when $n = 0$).
nodes.title: Riemann sum

nodes.summary: If $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ is a partition of $[a, b]$, then $x_{i+1} - x_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ with $0 \le i < n$.
nodes.title: Subintervals of a partition have nonnegative length

nodes.summary: If $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ is a partition of $[a, b]$, then the lengths of its subintervals sum to the length of the interval: $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (x_{i+1} - x_i) = b - a$.
nodes.title: Subinterval lengths of a partition telescope

nodes.summary: Every tag $\xi_k$ of a tagged partition of $[a, b]$ lies in $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Tags of a tagged partition lie in the interval

nodes.summary: A tagged partition of $[a, b]$ is a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ together with a choice of a tag $\xi_k \in [x_{k-1}, x_k]$ in each subinterval, for $k = 1, \dots, n$.
nodes.title: Tagged partition

Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
